reference_prefix: In 1917, a number of soldiers were diagnosed with the flu and were treated at Saint Roche's Sanitarium before being sent to the front. The next year, the 1918 Influenza pandemic devastated the globe. In 1928, the facility was upgraded with new medical equipment and renamed Saint Roche's Hospital. During WWII the island remained largely untouched by the fighting, though a section of the original monastery was inadvertently damaged by an American bomber when its bomb release system failed.
